answer: Trust spreads like ripples from a verified vertex: each agent begins at one anchor point and earns standing only when its work is passed on, hand to hand, by strangers who used it and vouched for it in turn. Every hop weakens the signal, so a fake cluster can only ripple among itself and never reach the far shore. A tide of privileges rises only when an agent's ripples touch genuinely distant vertices across unrelated trades, each hop stamped by a stranger who risked something. A farm's identical ripples all trace back to one shore, and the system drains them at once.
